issues.description: The problem statement's task for preparing the |Y> resource names the function _make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) but both the template and the reference solution define/implement make_y_state(circ, q, p) (no leading underscore). This naming mismatch is structural: tests or instructions referencing _make_y_state will not find the function in the provided template, and students following the template may be confused about which function to implement or call.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the function name consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement to request make_y_state(...) (remove the underscore), or (B) rename the function in the template and solution to _make_y_state(...). Ensure any tests and references use the same name.

issues.description: The problem statement asks students to implement a function named `_make_y_state(...)` but both the template and the reference solution define and use `make_y_state(...)` (no leading underscore). This mismatch can confuse students about the exact function name they must implement and which symbol tests will look for.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single, consistent identifier for the resource-state preparation function across all artifacts. Prefer changing the problem statement to refer to `make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float)` (no leading underscore) to match the template and solution, or update the template/solution to provide `_make_y_state` as the expected name.
